title: Filsuvez in Infants With Dystrophic or Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa
official: A Pilot Open-Label Trial Assessing Safety of Filsuvez in Patients With Dystrophic or Junctional Epidermolysis Bullosa Under Age 6 Months
summary: This pilot study will evaluate the safety and tolerability of Filsuvez, a topical gel, in newborns and infants younger than 6 months with dystrophic or junctional epidermolysis bullosa. Filsuvez is approved for patients 6 months of age and older but has not been studied in this younger population. Participants will receive Filsuvez for 180 days and will be followed with clinical assessments, laboratory testing, caregiver questionnaires, telephone contacts, and standardized photographs. The study will also explore changes in wound size, disease activity, pain, and family burden during and after treatment.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

1. Confirmed junctional epidermolysis bullosa or dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa diagnosis based on genetic and clinical evaluation.
2. Newborns and infants aged 5 months or younger at enrollment.
3. Ability of the parent or legal guardian to complete telephone assessments and comply with study procedures, as determined by the investigator.
4. Written informed consent from the parent or legal guardian.

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Systemic infection, septicemia, or sepsis at enrollment.
2. Systemic antibiotics for a wound-related infection within 7 days before enrollment.
3. Current wound infection.
4. Investigational therapy or systemic treatment that could interfere with wound healing within 30 days before enrollment.
5. Systemic or topical steroids, except inhaled or ophthalmic steroids, within 2 weeks before enrollment.
6. Enrollment in another interventional study or treatment with an investigational drug within 4 weeks before enrollment.
7. Immunosuppressive therapy or cytotoxic chemotherapy within 60 days before enrollment.
8. Allergy or hypersensitivity to Filsuvez, birch triterpenes, sunflower oil, or another product component.
9. Severe malnutrition or another condition that may compromise wound healing.
10. Likely need for major surgery during the study.
11. Inability to follow study procedures or scheduled follow-up.
12. Immediate family member of the investigational team.
